answer: Suppose a buyer commissions a sonnet about a sable fox beside the tide. Escrow one fixed reward under a unique job ID, and release it only once for an accepted deliverable; never pay signup bonuses or per-account participation fees. A swarm of aliases cannot multiply that job's payout. Require each competing submission to lock a refundable bond until review, making a flood costly in tied-up capital. This limits reward farming, but rich bidders can still crowd out rivals and a dishonest buyer can abuse subjective review.
